newsitem.title: UK: Legal & General outperforms insurance firms.
newsitem.headline: Legal & General outperforms insurance firms.

text.p: Shares in Legal & General Group Plc were benefiting on Tuesday from a continued move into financial stocks amid the ongoing flotation of British building societies, dealers said.
Legal & General shares were up 14.5 pence, or 3.55 percent, to 423p by 0915 GMT in volume of 2.0 million while the FTSE-100 index was 7.0 points, or 0.16 percent, higher at 4396.7.
"Nobody wants to be underweight in this sector," a trader a European bank based here said.
The insurance sector was generally firmer.
Investment funds have been increasing their weighting in financial stocks in anticipation of the entry into the FTSE-100 mutually-owned insurers like Norwich Union.

Private investors were being advised to hang on to their Halifax and Woolwich shares after sharp post-flotation gains in Alliance & Leicester Plc last week, making it likely investment funds will find it even more difficult to accumulate all the shares they want in the new quoted groups.
Banks were also seen as offering secure earnings insulated from the squeeze from the rising pound that has afflicted many industrial stocks and overseas earners.
